volt: In the International System of Units, the derived unit of electrical potential and electromotive force (voltage); the potential difference across a conductor when a current of one ampere uses one watt of power. Symbol: V
voltage: (electricity) The difference in electrostatic potential between two points in space, especially between live and neutral conductors or the earth.
volume: A three-dimensional measure of space that comprises a length, a width and a height. It is measured in units of cubic centimeters in metric, cubic inches or cubic feet in English measurement.
voluntary: Done by design or intention; intentional.
volunteer: One who enters into, or offers themselves for, any service of their own free will, especially when done without pay.
vomit: The regurgitated former contents of a stomach; vomitus.
(intransitive) To regurgitate or eject the contents of the stomach through the mouth; puke.
voodoo: Any of a group of related religious practices found chiefly in and around the Caribbean, particularly in Haiti and Louisiana.
voronezh: A city, the administrative center of Voronezh Oblast, Russia.
vortex: A whirlwind, whirlpool, or similarly moving matter in the form of a spiral or column.
vote: A formalized choice on legally relevant measures such as employment or appointment to office or a proceeding about a legal dispute.
(intransitive) To cast a vote; to assert a formalized choice in an election.
votic: A nearly extinct Finno-Ugric language spoken in Ingria.
voting: action of the verb to vote
voucher: A piece of paper or other token that entitles the holder to a discount, or that can be exchanged for goods and services.
vow: A solemn promise to perform some act, or behave in a specified manner, especially a promise to live and act in accordance with the rules of a religious order.
(ambitransitive) To make a vow; to promise.
vowel: (phonetics) A sound produced by the vocal cords with relatively little restriction of the oral cavity, forming the prominent sound of a syllable.
vroom: (informal) To move with great speed; to zoom.
vulcan: (Roman god) The god of volcanoes and fire, especially the forge, also the patron of all craftsmen, especially blacksmiths. The Roman counterpart of Hephaestus.
vulcanization: A process by which rubber is hardened using heat and sulphur.
vulnerability: (uncountable) The state of being vulnerable; susceptibility to attack or injury, either physical or emotional; the state or condition of being weak or poorly defended.
vulnerable: More or most likely to be exposed to the chance of being attacked or harmed, either physically or emotionally.
vulpecula: (constellation) A faint autumn constellation in the northern sky.
vulture: Any of several carrion-eating birds of the families Accipitridae and Cathartidae.
vulva: (anatomy) The external female genitalia of humans and other placental mammals, which includes the clitoris, labia, and vulval vestibule/vulvar opening.
vytkiv: A village in Hoshcha settlement hromada, Rivne Raion, Rivne Oblast, Ukraine, founded in 1765.
vítkov: A town in okres Opava, Moravia–Silesia, the Czech Republic, first mentioned in 1301.
